author: Contributor 41
about: Kiln's year on Cloudflare (journeys/customer-life.outline.md): Open Autonomy's deploy token and wrangler deploys (Durable Objects among them), R2 storage behind its link, media and recording apps (Dub's, Postiz's, RH2's code paths), a public bucket domain, its customers' own domains (Twenty's custom hostnames), Turnstile on sign-up and booking (Cal.com's, Rallly's, LibreChat's), a rolled deploy token and a revoked R2 token, the account read back, and the old bucket closed.

steps.name: Monday 5 January, 09:00: Kiln moves its site and its media to Cloudflare
The World: Mina signs up at dash.cloudflare.com with her email and a password (the dashboard's sign-up, which no API makes)
The World: her sign-up makes the account Kiln, Mina its Super Administrator, and the World's application its account token and R2 keys (the credential door)
Open Autonomy's setup opens the API token page pre-filled from its template URL; signed out, the dashboard sends Mina to log in first
The login page shows its form, the token page to come back to in its next field
She logs in, and the dashboard takes her back to the token page
The form arrives filled in from the template: the name and the three permission groups

expect.contains: Workers Scripts Write,Account Settings Read,User Details Read

steps.name: She restricts it to Kiln's account and creates it; the page shows the token once
Pasted with its last characters cut off, a token is refused, and setup stops to ask again
She corrects the pasted value; setup verifies it before putting it in the repository production environment: active
Monday 5 January, 11:30: the repository is released for the first time, and its deploy workflow runs wrangler deploy
wrangler reads the account's workers.dev subdomain: the account has none yet, so the deploy cannot put the Worker there
Mina registers kiln.workers.dev for the account, as an owner does before a first deploy
The Worker's cache bucket is made through the API, as the platform's deploy makes its own
Before binding CACHE, wrangler reads the bucket the account created
Monday 5 January, 11:45: the workflow runs wrangler deploy again
wrangler reads the Worker's latest deployment: there is no Worker yet, which it takes as a first deploy
…and its service, for the migration tag it holds: none
It reads the account's workers.dev subdomain: kiln
The site has static assets: an upload session over their manifest names the one file to send
An upload sent with the deploy token, not the session's JWT, is refused
The file goes up with the session's JWT: every file is in, and the answer is the completion token
wrangler uploads the Worker: its module, its metadata with the R2 bucket and the assets bound, the completion token among them
steps.body:
------wranglerkiln
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="metadata"
Content-Type: application/json

{"main_module":"index.js","compatibility_date":"2026-01-05","bindings":[{"name":"CACHE","type":"r2_bucket","bucket_name":"kiln-site-cache"},{"name":"ASSETS","type":"assets"}],"assets":{"jwt":"{assets_done}","config":{"html_handling":"auto-trailing-slash"}},"observability":{"enabled":true}}
------wranglerkiln
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="index.js"; filename="index.js"
Content-Type: application/javascript+module

export default { async fetch(request, env) { return env.ASSETS.fetch(request); } };
------wranglerkiln--
